auditSample.textSample: Created in Augsburg around 1600 and attributed to the master clockmaker Hans Schottheim, the Bacchusautomat (KK 959) depicts a triumphant procession of Bacchus, the ancient Roman god of wine, theatre, and revelry. Powered entirely by clockwork, it moved across the banquet table while its internal mechanism produced music, eventually coming to a stop before a guest, who was then expected to drink from the detachable goat’s head-shaped vessel. These intricate Renaissance automata are regarded as important precursors in the history of robotics, revealing how early modern craftsmen transformed gears, cams, springs, and mechanical music into complex automated performances. #mechanicalart #automat
